extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary educational institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and legal counsel implementing Title IX
extracted.subtask_description: Interpreting and implementing final Title IX regulatory definitions and related compliance requirements for educational recipients, including how to identify and respond to sex-based harassment and specified offenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spending Clause notice / reliance on notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies have authority to define the contours of the Spending Clause contract with recipients through their regulations; the notice-and-comment rulemaking process (e.g., the July 2022 NPRM) provides the notice required by Pennhurst and related precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients of Federal financial assistance agree to comply with Title IX obligations, including regulatory requirements, as a condition of receiving funds; therefore recipients should have anticipated the final definition becoming effective when they continued to accept Federal funds. The Department rejects the view that mere historic practice alone demonstrates whether recipients were given notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hostile environment sex-based harassment — core elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined as unwelcome sex-based conduct that, based on the totality of the circumstances, is subjectively and objectively offensive and is so severe or pervasive that it limits or denies a person's ability to participate in or benefit from the recipient's education program or activity (i.e., creates a hostile environment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a hostile environment has been created is a fact-specific inquiry considering: the degree to which the conduct affected the complainant's ability to access the education program or activity; type, frequency, and duration of the conduct; the parties' ages, roles within the program or activity, previous interactions, and other relevant factors about each party; location and context of the conduct; and other sex-based harassment in the recipient's program or activity. The definition contemplates and requires application of administrator judgment and is intended to be workable in elementary and secondary settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolated-event threshold for hostile environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct that is an isolated event must be so severe that it limits or denies participation in an activity to constitute hostile environment sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes that a single instance of severe student-to-student harassment could have the systemic effect of denying a student equal access; administrative enforcement can address such single acts even where private suits for monetary damages may apply a different standard (Davis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct must be sex-based (on the basis of sex)
rubrics_metrics.description: For conduct to be prohibited under Title IX as sex-based harassment, it must be 'on the basis of sex' and not merely a circumstance in which students happen to be different genders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement narrows scope of implicated conduct; Department cites Oncale to explain that not all inter-gender harassment is automatically discrimination because of sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific offenses included as sex-based harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'sex-based harassment' includes textual definitions of specific offenses: sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, and stalking (largely aligned with the Clery Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department included textual definitions rather than cross-references to the Clery Act to improve readability and reduce the need to consult other statutes. If statutory definitions change in the future, the Department may consider technical updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific offenses need not satisfy hostile-environment elements or unwelcomeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific offenses (sexual assault, dating violence, domestic violence, stalking) need not satisfy the elements of severity or pervasiveness or subjective and objective offensiveness, and they need not satisfy the element of unwelcomeness, to constitute sex-based harassment under these regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors the treatment in the 2020 amendments and means an enumerated specific offense can constitute sex-based harassment even if it would not meet the hostile-environment multi-factor test; the reference to sexual assault (based on Clery Act) introduces the concept of consent as relevant to that specific offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual assault definition (Clery Act / FBI UCR alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of sexual assault in the final regulations mirrors the Clery Act's statutory definition which tracks the FBI UCR/NIBRS: sex offenses include Rape, Sodomy, Sexual Assault With An Object, Fondling, Incest, and Statutory Rape, i.e., offenses occurring 'without the consent of the victim.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to rewrite the FBI's UCR text in the Title IX regulations but retains language tracking the Clery Act and VAWA 2022. The use of terms 'forcible or nonforcible' is retained for statutory consistency and is not meant to imply force is required. Sexual gratification is not an element required by the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent — Department will not set a federal definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department is not itself defining 'consent' nor requiring recipients to adopt a particular definition of 'consent' for Title IX purposes; a recipient may choose to define 'consent' in its policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added a note explaining the Assistant Secretary will not require a recipient to adopt a particular definition of consent. Recipients may consider state law and consistency with disability laws when defining consent. The Department declines to prohibit or require particular definitions (including affirmative consent). Institutions may provide examples and trainings to clarify their policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of gathering evidence and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.45(f)(1), the recipient—and not the parties—must gather sufficient evidence to determine whether sex discrimination occurred; the recipient cannot shift the burden of proof or the burden of gathering evidence to a respondent or complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations require the recipient to gather evidence; recipients may not require respondents to prove consent nor require complainants to prove absence of consent. Training must reflect the recipient's policy and any definition of consent the recipient chooses to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability / scope of Title IX jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX applies to sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment, occurring under a recipient's education program or activity in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sex-based harassment (including specific offenses) occurs outside a recipient's education program or activity, Title IX does not apply; however, a recipient is required to address a hostile environment that exists under its program or activity even when some contributing conduct occurred outside the program or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dating violence definition aligned to VAWA 2022
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of dating violence in the final regulations has been revised to align fully with VAWA 2022: violence committed by a person who is or has been in a social relationship of a romantic or intimate nature with the victim, with relationship existence determined by length, type, and frequency of interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition does not require that dating violence be a 'crime of violence.' The Department declined proposals to combine dating and domestic violence definitions or to add additional VAWA victim-services language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic violence definition: selected alignment and omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's final definition of domestic violence aligns with parts of VAWA 2022 but omits language related to 'victim services' that the Department determined is not applicable to Title IX; the phrase 'of violence' was removed to better align with VAWA 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the final definition references crimes, coercive or controlling behavior that does not fit the domestic-violence definition may still constitute sex-based harassment if it is sex-based and meets the hostile-environment elements. Recipients should be aware that other Federal agencies (e.g., HUD) may use different domestic-violence definitions and recipients must comply with any applicable overlapping regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex-trafficking and related conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to add 'sex trafficking' to the list of specific offenses (because it is not listed in the Clery Act), but clarified that acts associated with sex-trafficking may fall within the definition of hostile environment sex-based harassment if they meet the elements of that definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sex-trafficking is both a federal crime (e.g., 18 U.S.C. 1591) and a grave concern; conduct need not be enumerated to be covered if it otherwise meets the hostile-environment elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of textual definitions versus cross-references (policy clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department opted to include textual definitions of the Clery Act offenses within the Title IX regulations rather than cross-referencing other statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: improve readability, reduce need for recipients to consult other statutes, and reflect that some statutory provisions are not applicable in the Title IX context. The Department will assess possible future technical updates if statutory definitions change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special considerations for elementary and secondary students and students with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may consider a student's age or developmental level when defining consent; when a complainant or respondent is an elementary or secondary student with a disability, the Title IX Coordinator must consult with members of the student's IEP team and Section 504 team to ensure compliance with IDEA and Section 504.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain evidence (e.g., treatment records) may be relevant to capacity to consent, but the final regulations restrict use of such records in grievance procedures unless the party voluntarily provides written consent (§106.45(b)(7)(ii)). Training required under the regulations should include any definitions used by the recipient, including definitions of consent if adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology consistency and allowance for recipient-level clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Department retains certain statutory terms (e.g., 'forcible or nonforcible') for consistency with Clery Act/Victim statutes, recipients are permitted—and encouraged—to provide examples, scenarios, and trainings in their policies to clarify terms and definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes variation across authorities (FBI UCR, Clery Act, AAP, state law) and intentionally provides flexibility to recipients to adopt clarifying language and examples, consistent with applicable law.
